correction.text: the island of Naxos, largely captured in 1207 and entirely occupied in 1210

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1207-1209: Cliopatria's row begins in 1210. 'The Duchy of the Archipelago was created in 1207 by the Venetian nobleman Marco Sanudo', who 'arrived with eight galleys and largely captured the island' of Naxos; 'With the entire island occupied in 1210' he went on to the other Cyclades. A 20 km disc around Naxos is the researcher's reading of 'the island'.

keyframe_review.note: The shape is corrected: Cliopatria's 1,233 km2, resolved on the project's grid, is four cells, at Kea, Andros (two cells) and Naxos, which leaves out most of the Cyclades and includes Andros, 'held by Dandolo' and so not in the duchy. The page says the duchy 'included all the Cyclades (except Mykonos and Tinos)' with Sanudo's personal holdings Paros, Antiparos, Milos, Sifnos, Kythnos, Ios, Amorgos, Kimolos, Sikinos, Syros and Pholegandros. No area on the page. Holds 1210-1277; Licario's Byzantines take most islands 1277-c. 1280 (see _1278). Fixed after review: the spec had subtracted only a 22 km disc at Andros, so it contradicted the page's 'except Mykonos and Tinos'; discs at Tinos (25.16 E 37.59 N, 14 km) and Mykonos (25.36 E 37.45 N, 10 km) are now subtracted too (on the project's grid the Cyclades region is six cells and none lies on Tinos or Mykonos, so the cell count is unchanged). The page does not say whether Andros, held by Dandolo, was in the duchy; it stays out as a reading.

correction.text: Naxos and Paros, the islands Marco II kept

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1278-1309: Licario's Byzantine fleet took Karystos (1276), Skopelos (1277), Skyros, Skiathos and Amorgos ('soon after' 1277) and later undated Kythera, Kea, Santorini, Sifnos and Serifos (Licario page); the duchy page says Marco II 'lost many of the islands, except Naxos and Paros' in the late 13th century and that the Byzantines 'relinquished control of their gains in 1310'. Only Naxos and Paros are drawn as certain; the year for each Cycladic island is not on either page (see ledger, confidence 1). Moved from 1277 to 1278 after review: the only year the Licario page gives for a duchy island is none (Skopelos 1277 was a Ghisi island; Amorgos 'soon after'; Kea, Santorini 'later'; Sifnos and Serifos after the Battle of Vatondas, late 1279 or early 1280), so 1278 bridges the silence.

correction.text: Naxos and Paros, the islands Marco II kept

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria's 1305-1313 shape (664.5 km2; two cells at 24.76-24.85 E, 37.81-37.96 N, which is Andros) is not the duchy: the page puts Andros with the Dandolo, not the duchy, and says the duchy kept at least Naxos and Paros after Licario, with the rest returning in 1310. The correction gives Naxos and Paros for 1305-1309 and the full duchy from 1310 (see _1310).

correction.text: all the Cyclades except Mykonos and Tinos (the Ghisi) and, as a reading, Andros (Dandolo)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1310-1579: after the Byzantines 'relinquished control of their gains in 1310' the duchy again 'included all the Cyclades (except Mykonos and Tinos)'. The page records no further territorial change to 1579 (the Catalan raid of 1317 took nothing, Tinos and Mykonos stayed Venetian, the Gozzadini held Sifnos to 1617), so the 1210 shape is carried; the islands Cliopatria's other rows may take in these centuries (Venice, the Ottomans) are not checked. Unverified: page budget. Page re-read 2026-10-19 for island-by-island change: the duchy page dates only the 1317 Catalan raid (no land taken), the 1383 Crispo coup, the 1418 Venetian vassalage, the 1537 Ottoman suzerainty, the 1566 deposition and 1579; it gives no dated change for Naxos, Paros, Milos, Andros, Mykonos or Santorini, and says the Gozzadini 'survived as lords of Sifnos and other little islands in the Cyclades until 1617' and Tinos stayed Venetian (1714/15). No territorial change to 1579 is therefore recorded.

ledger.note: 1207: Marco Sanudo founds the Duchy of the Archipelago on Naxos. 'The Duchy of the Archipelago was created in 1207 by the Venetian nobleman Marco Sanudo'; he arrived with eight galleys and 'largely captured the island' of Naxos, the capital and headquarters; Sanudo recognised the Latin Emperor, not Venice, as overlord. Cliopatria begins in 1210, when 'the entire island [was] occupied'.

ledger.note: 1210: with Naxos entirely occupied Sanudo conquers Melos and the rest of the Cyclades. 'With the entire island occupied in 1210, Sanudo went on to conquer Melos and the rest of the Cyclades'; his personal holdings were Paros, Antiparos, Milos, Sifnos, Kythnos, Ios, Amorgos, Kimolos, Sikinos, Syros and Pholegandros; Mykonos and Tinos stayed with the Ghisi and Andros with Dandolo. The page dates only 1210 for Naxos, so the island conquests that follow are undated.

ledger.note: 1278: Licario's Byzantines take most of the duchy's islands (bridging year, moved from 1277 after review). The duchy page: Marco II 'lost many of the islands, except Naxos and Paros' to Byzantine forces under the admiral Licario 'in the late 13th century' (no year); the Marco II Sanudo page: he 'lost some of his islands to the Byzantine Empire early in his reign'. The Licario page: Karystos 1276, Skopelos 1277 (a Ghisi island, not the duchy's), Skyros, Skiathos and Amorgos 'soon after', then Kythera and Antikythera (Venetian vassals, not the duchy's), 'later Kea, Astypalaia, and Santorini', and Sifnos and Serifos after the Battle of Vatondas (late 1279 or early 1280), with Licario vanishing c. 1280. The duchy's islands therefore fell between 1277 and c. 1280 and 1278 is a bridge; the islands lost are the researcher's reading of 'many of the islands'.

ledger.note: 1310: the Byzantines give up their Cycladic gains. 'they relinquished control of their gains in 1310' (duchy page); the Licario page says rather that the Byzantine conquests 'proved temporary only' and that 'the Byzantines were gradually evicted by the Venetians and the other Latin lords'. The duchy page's year is followed. The Marco II Sanudo page says he 'recovered them two decades later' (no year), which from the late 1270s would be the 1290s, a decade earlier than the duchy page's 1310; the duchy page's dated year is kept.

1383: the Crispo overthrow the Sanudo heirs. 'the Crispo family led an armed insurrection and overthrew Sanudo's heirs'; Francesco I Crispo ruled 1383-97. The duchy continues under a new dynasty, same land.

1566: Selim II deposes the last Crispo duke. Giacomo IV Crispo was 'deposed in 1566 by Ottoman Sultan Selim II'; Joseph Nasi, a Portuguese Jew, ruled as the Sultan's appointee (1566-79). Ottoman suzerainty over the duchy had begun in 1537 (infobox) and Venetian vassalage in 1418; the Ottoman and Venetian dossiers should carry the vassal events.

ledger.note: 1579: the Ottomans annex the duchy. 'Expropriated by Murad III: 1579' (infobox); successor the Sanjak of Naksa Berre. The page says the Gozzadini 'survived as lords of Sifnos and other little islands in the Cyclades until 1617' after the annexation (Sifnos was one of Sanudo's personal holdings, so it is inside the region drawn) and Tinos stayed Venetian to 1714/15 (outside the duchy).

notes: Written 2026-10-19 by eu-05-e from two pages (budget 1-2). Scope extended beyond Cliopatria: the Cliopatria row is 1210-1313 but the page runs the duchy 1207-1579 (infobox 'Expropriated by Murad III: 1579'); 1207-1209 and 1310-1579 are new keyframes on the single duchy page and are marked unverified for territorial changes. Cliopatria rows: the 1210-1304 shape resolves on the project grid to cells at Kea, Andros (two) and Naxos and the 1305-1313 shape to the two Andros cells only (664.5 km2); the page puts Andros with the Dandolo, outside the duchy, so the 1305 shape is 'wrong'. Cliopatria therefore draws no duchy for 1314-1579; the Venice or Ottoman rows may draw the Cyclades then (not checked). Not settled: the years in which each island fell to Licario (the Licario page dates Karystos 1276, Skopelos 1277, Amorgos soon after, the rest undated) and in which they returned (duchy page 1310; Licario page 'gradually evicted'); the status of Santorini and Kea (not mentioned on the duchy page; the Licario page lists them among the islands Licario took); Andros after the Dandolo; the 1494-1500 and 1511-1517 gaps in the page's ruler list (the list was read through WebFetch and may omit entries). Overlordships for other dossiers (the pages give years): Latin Empire from 1207 (Sanudo recognised the Latin Emperor); Achaea's William of Villehardouin from 1248 ('nominally granted by Baldwin II'); the Angevins of Naples from 1278; Venice from 1418; the Ottomans from 1537. Gazetteer: Naxos, Paros, Andros and Kea are not places in the gazetteer; lon/lat discs are used and the 'Cyclades' region (six cells) stands for the archipelago. Cliopatria's 1,233 km2 cannot be compared with the page: it gives no area. Review fixes 2026-10-19: Tinos and Mykonos discs added to every Cyclades spec (the page's 'except Mykonos and Tinos'); the Licario loss moved from 1277 to 1278 (confidence 1, bridging 1277-c. 1280); the Marco II page's 'two decades later' recovery conflicts with the duchy page's 1310 and is not followed.
